title: Counting in 2s, 5s and 10s
examples: Can you show me what comes after 30 when counting by fives?
How do I find the next number if I am counting by tens?
What is the pattern if we start at 10 and count by twos?

explain.say: Today we are learning to skip count. This means we count by a number, jumping over others. We can count by twos, fives, and tens.
Let us try counting by twos. We start at two and keep adding two each time. Two, four, six, eight, ten. See how we jump two spaces each time?
Now we count by fives. Start at five and add five each time. Five, ten, fifteen, twenty, twenty-five. These numbers are special.
Next we count by tens. We start at ten and add ten each time. Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty. These are easy to remember.
We can also use a hundred square to see these patterns. Look at the top row. These numbers are always counting by tens.

faq.a: It means counting by a set number instead of counting by one each time. You are jumping over the numbers in between.
asks: What does it mean to count by twos?

faq.q: Why do we learn to count by fives?
faq.a: Counting by fives helps us know how many groups of five fit into a number. It is very useful for money counting.

faq.q: How do I find the next number when counting by tens?
faq.a: You just add ten to the number you are currently on. For example, after fifty, you say sixty.
asks: What comes after 70 counting by tens?
How do I jump to the next ten?

faq.q: Can I use the 100 square for all these counts?
faq.a: Yes, the 100 square shows patterns for all these counts. You can see the jumps for twos, fives, and tens.
asks: Does the 100 square help with twos?
Is the 100 square only for tens?

faq.q: If I count by twos, do I always land on an even number?
faq.a: Yes, when you start at two and count by twos, every number you say will be even. Even numbers are always divisible by two.
asks: Are all numbers I say when counting by twos even?
What kind of numbers do I get when I count by twos?

facts: Counting by twos means adding two to the previous number each time.
Counting by fives is useful for counting money in groups of five.
Counting by tens means adding ten to the previous number each time.
The 100 square helps us see number patterns clearly.

quiz.why: We are counting by twos, so we add two to eight to get ten.

wrong.0: This number is too big for this small pattern.
wrong.2: You added one instead of two. Remember to jump by two each time.
wrong.3: You added four. We only add two in this pattern.

quiz.why: We are counting by fives, so we add five to twenty to get twenty-five.

wrong.0: This number is much too large for this pattern.
wrong.2: You added ten. We need to add only five.
wrong.3: This number is not a multiple of five.

quiz.why: This pattern counts by tens, so we add ten to thirty to get forty.

wrong.0: You added five. We must add ten for this pattern.
wrong.1: You added one. We are skipping numbers.
wrong.2: This number is too big for this simple pattern.
